entries.text: Chocolate contains theobromine, which is toxic to dogs and cats and can cause vomiting, a racing heart, tremors and seizures. Darker chocolate is more dangerous.
Grapes and raisins can cause sudden kidney failure in dogs, even in small amounts.
Onions, garlic, leeks and chives damage red blood cells and can cause anemia in dogs and cats.
Xylitol, found in sugar-free gum and some peanut butters, can cause a dangerous drop in blood sugar and liver failure in dogs.
Puppies and kittens start core vaccinations (rabies, DHPP for dogs, FVRCP for cats) at 6-8 weeks of age, with repeat doses every 3-4 weeks until about 16 weeks.
Adult pets need booster shots every 1 or 3 years, depending on the vaccine type and local law. Your vet will set the exact schedule.
Difficulty breathing, pale gums, sudden collapse, seizures, heavy bleeding or eating a known toxin need emergency veterinary care right away.
Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to 2 hours of activity a day depending on breed, age and health. Puppies and senior dogs do better with shorter, gentler sessions.
Indoor cats benefit from two or three short play sessions (10-15 minutes) a day with toys that mimic hunting, like wands and balls.
Feed a complete, balanced diet made for your pet's life stage and adjust portions to keep a healthy body shape. Your vet can give you a daily calorie target.
